name: Semiprime_Single_Factor_Extraction

phase_0.boundary_condition: The horn torus with logarithmic encoding (R=r=1.8, φ=log₂n/7, θ=k/7) that contains the complete factorization space up to N=128, where multiplication becomes translation and every semiprime's factor pair lies on the k=1 reference ring as a chord triangle.

⊢.chosen_element: uninitialized semiprime N awaiting factor extraction
⊢.justification: The void state before any prime candidate engages the divisibility test; N exists on the k=1 ring at φ=log₂N/7 but its factors are unknown.

⊣.chosen_element: verified factor pair (p, q) with p·q=N and zero remainder
⊣.justification: The closed boundary where extraction completes: both factors are fixed, the product reconstructs N exactly, and the chord triangle p-q-N on the k=1 ring is fully resolved.

≻.chosen_element: advance to next prime candidate along its helix
≻.justification: Forward morphism moving along the prime helix (φ advances by log₂p/7 per step, θ by 1/7) to test successive powers or the next prime in the well list.

≺.justification: Contravariant descent when a candidate fails: the register clears, the helix position reverses, and the search continues with the next candidate without losing the semiprime anchor.

⋈.chosen_element: compose division test with cofactor computation and verification
⋈.justification: Sequential chaining: candidate p divides N → compute q=N/p → verify p·q=N → confirm zero remainder → each step feeds the next.

⊙.justification: Identity operation where the extracted pair recognizes itself as the exact factorization: the semiprime knows its own factors through the multiplicative closure on the torus.

∈.chosen_element: divisibility test: does candidate p divide N?
∈.justification: The fork that opens two arms: T-arm where p|N (factor found) and F-arm where p∤N (continue search). This is the fundamental decision point in factor extraction.

∋.chosen_element: rejoin after divisibility test with result
∋.justification: The arms rejoin carrying either the extracted factor pair (T-arm) or the continued search state (F-arm). Conflicting results (multiple candidates) fuse to B, holding both factor and cofactor simultaneously during verification.

⊤.justification: Affirmative arm: the division succeeds, p is a true factor, q=N/p is computed, and the factor pair is established.

⊥.chosen_element: candidate p does not divide N (remainder≠0)
⊥.justification: Negative arm: the division fails, p is rejected, the helix advances to the next candidate, and the search continues.

⊞.chosen_element: hold factor p and cofactor q simultaneously during verification
⊞.justification: Paradice state: both the extracted factor and its implicit complement are held live (B-state) while the product p·q is checked against N, before fixation commits the pair.

⊡.chosen_element: permanent record of the extracted factor pair in the factorization log
⊡.justification: Irreversible ROM fixation: once verified, the factor pair (p,q) is appended to the immutable record; the semiprime is resolved and cannot return to unfactored state without exponential recomposition.

phase_2.split_input: semiprime N on k=1 ring and candidate prime p from helix well
split_outputs: T-arm: p divides N → factor found
F-arm: p does not divide N → advance helix
phase_2.fuse_result: either verified factor pair (p,q) held in B-state during verification, or updated search state with next candidate queued
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: Semiprime N placed on k=1 ring at φ=log₂N/7; no candidates tested; helix position at first prime well
phase_3.true_description: Factor p extracted, cofactor q=N/p computed, product verified p·q=N, zero remainder confirmed, chord triangle p-q-N resolved on k=1 ring
phase_3.false_description: Candidate p rejected (remainder≠0); helix advanced to next prime; N unchanged on k=1 ring; search continues
phase_3.both_description: Factor p and cofactor q held simultaneously in verification: p·q≡N checked, both arms live, B-state persists until IFIX commits the pair or AREV clears for next candidate

steps.domain_action: Initialize void semiprime N on k=1 ring at φ=log₂N/7, θ=2π/7; prime well list loaded (primes ≤128); helix positions zeroed
Self-reference N as the target semiprime; establish holographic state V=L(x)∧selfmodel(x)∧x∈V (HOLOGRAPHIC_STATE)
Open divisibility test fork — candidate prime p from first helix well enters (BRIDGE_EXIST: ∃y∈x(|y|∼|x|))
T-arm anchor — test if p divides N (remainder=0)
On T-arm — advance to cofactor computation q=N/p (BRIDGE_COMP: Fun(x,y)∧Nat(y,z)→Fun(x,z))
Compose division result with cofactor derivation
Self-check p·q ≡ N on torus (multiplication as rotation by φ₀=log₂p/7)
Enter B-state — hold both p and q simultaneously during verification (PHI_C: ξ→∞∧μ∘δ=id)
Fix verified factor pair (p,q) in permanent record
F-arm anchor — p does not divide N (remainder≠0)
On F-arm — backtrack: clear register, retain open fork frame
Advance helix to next prime candidate (φ advances by log₂p_next/7)
Nested fork — test next candidate (inner split for each prime)
Inner T-arm — candidate divides N
Compute cofactor
Chain verification
Product self-check
Hold both factors
Fix pair
Close inner fork — rejoin with factor pair or continue (SEQAX: seq!(f,g)∧⟨→⟩(f,g,τ)∧¬⟨→⟩(g,f,τ))
Inner F-arm — candidate fails
Clear register, retain outer fork
Advance helix
Close outer fork — rejoin search state
Compose sequential test results across all candidates
Top-level fork — factor found vs. search exhausted
Factor found arm — verified pair ready
Terminal anchor — close boundary with resolved semiprime (MOAT_CROSS: cross(x,y)∧¬meet(x,y))
Search exhausted arm — no factor found (N is prime, contradiction for semiprime)
Hold contradiction B-state (semiprime with no factors)
Record impossibility (should not occur for valid semiprime)
Close top-level fork
Final self-reference — extraction complete, N knows its factors
System boundary sealed — factor pair (p,q) fixed in log

phase_5.compiler_frontend: Logarithmic torus encoder mapping integers n to helix coordinates (φ=log₂n/7, θ=k/7); translates factorization intent into geometric traversal
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Prime helix traversal passes candidate factors to division test; division test returns remainder to helix controller; verified pair passes to fixation log
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Toroidal coordinate register stores current (φ, θ) on helix; factorization log (append-only) stores fixed (p,q) pairs; search state stack retains open fork frames
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Cinematic timeline phases (11 chapters, t∈[0,99]) control layer revelation: semiprime triangles (stage≥4), negative sheet (stage≥5), power-set residues (stage≥6), binary connections (stage≥7), cardioid sweep (stage≥8), multiplier rotation (stage=9)

phase_6.cycle_cost: One division test per candidate prime (modular arithmetic); helix advancement (coordinate update); verification (multiplication check)
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Semiprime N on k=1 ring; prime helix at candidate p; search state open; factorization log unchanged
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Either factor pair (p,q) fixed in log (IFIX) with N resolved, or helix advanced to next candidate with fork frame retained
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The torus rotation is reversible (multiplication by 2^e is rigid rotation); each divisibility test is deterministic with no information loss; the search explores a finite, fixed set of candidates; fixation is append-only but the total state space (all semiprimes ≤128) is bounded and pre-determined.

grounding_reasoning:
⊣=𐑥: The divisibility test fork (FSPLIT) creates a cyclic closure where the T-arm (factor found) and F-arm (advance helix) rejoin at FFUSE, forming a figure-8 loop that iterates across prime candidates until the factor pair closes the boundary at TANCH.
⊢=𐑦: The extraction operates on the semiprime's bit-length as a scale-collapsed register where the horn torus boundary (φ=log₂N/7, θ=k/7) encodes the full factorization space losslessly, with multiplication as rigid rotation and the k=1 ring containing all candidate factors.
⊞=𐑳: The semiprime N (one composite) engages a sequence of single prime candidates (many) but resolves to exactly one factor p and its implicit cofactor q, an asymmetric 1-to-2 participation where one entity yields a specific pair.
⊡=𐑴: The factor's role is Z2-protected because the divisibility test fork creates a binary topological boundary (T-arm/F-arm) where extracting a factor forces a discrete partition (p|N vs p∤N) that cannot be continuously deformed without crossing the zero-remainder threshold.
⊙=⊙: The extraction operates at a sharp algebraic threshold where the divisibility test (remainder=0) creates scale-free correlations across the full factorization space, with maximal sensitivity to the precise divisor and no subcritical or supercritical regime.
⊥=𐑖: The ordered factor pair (p,q) with p<q establishes a persistent chiral asymmetry on the k=1 ring where the chord triangle orientation (smaller vs. larger prime) is structurally enforced by the logarithmic encoding and cannot be mirrored without changing the factorization identity.
≻=𐑑: The extraction irreversibly transforms the semiprime's composite structure into a resolved factor pair through the divisibility test, constituting a structural transformation that cannot be reversed without exponential recomposition of the original integer.
≺=𐑿: The extraction interface has a signed direction from the composite semiprime (donor) toward the extracted factor (acceptor) along the helix traversal, with no simultaneous reverse role or self-complementarity.
⋈=𐑐: The divisibility test is deterministic and exact: a correct factor divides the semiprime with zero remainder, transmitting the full factorization information with near-certainty and no probabilistic ambiguity.
⊤=𐑧: The factorization state is kinetically frozen with a high barrier: once a semiprime is factored, the result is mathematically irreversible and requires exponential computational effort to rearrange back to an unfactored state.
∈=𐑔: The extraction of a single factor instantly resolves the entire semiprime structure, propagating the correlation across the full integer (the cofactor is determined globally) with scale-free algebraic reach on the horn torus.
∋=𐑠: The extraction follows a strict sequential logic: the semiprime is engaged first, then candidate primes are tested in order along their helices, and only upon successful division is the cofactor resolved as the final partner.
